name: Act of March 3, 1891 ratifying the Crow agreement of 1890
promises: Royce records that the Crow ceded the part of their reservation lying west and south of a described line along the Yellowstone, Pryor Mountain and Bighorn River, except lands selected for individual Indians.
The Court of Claims records that the consideration was $946,000 to be disbursed for the benefit of the Crows.
today: In 1935 the Court of Claims, hearing Crow claims under a 1926 jurisdictional act that reached later agreements, said there had been no taking of Crow lands and that every cession was made for a consideration; it dismissed the petition. This was a ruling against the nation.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 942
Crow Nation v. United States, 81 Ct. Cl. 238 (1935)
sources.publisher: Caselaw Access Project, Harvard Law School

openQuestions: The Crow Tribe's Indian Claims Commission Docket 54 concerns the 1868 cession of Fort Laramie lands; no Commission claim about the 1891 cession was found.
Royce cites the act at 26 Stat. 1039; the Court of Claims cites 26 Stat. 989, 1040.
The Crow Tribe's own account of the 1891 cession was not located.
